reasoning_traces.think:
MRLEs define a general framework for estimating high-dimensional parameters by minimizing negative log-likelihood plus a regularization term. The core innovation lies in avoiding restrictive assumptions like sparsity or restricted eigenvalues. Instead, it leverages duality through the dual norm of the KL divergence gradient to derive finite-sample oracle inequalities. This allows for prediction guarantees even when traditional assumptions fail. In GSI, these principles enable robust Bayesian inference over complex sports datasets, while in GSE, they support adaptive regularization in dynamic state transitions. The dual norm control ensures that the regularization parameter adapts to empirical risk, preventing overfitting. Tensor applications extend this to structured data like player movement tensors or game outcome matrices, enabling more nuanced modeling of interactions. The failure mode occurs when empirical process bounds do not hold or when the regularizer lacks positive homogeneity.
